result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a lack of formal crossing infrastructure at a wide intersection. While sidewalks are present, the absence of marked crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and clear traffic control for the main roadway creates a hostile environment for people walking.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks at the intersection, leaving pedestrians without a designated or protected space to cross.

hazards.name: Restricted Sightlines
hazards.description: Parked vehicles close to the intersection corners obstruct the view between approaching drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs of both intersecting streets

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A vehicle is parked partially on the sidewalk/apron area, narrowing the available path for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side in front of the red building

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the intersection to improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The environment is a wide, multi-lane arterial with a painted bike lane but lacks visible marked crosswalks or pedestrian refuge islands. The scale of the roadway and lack of crossing infrastructure suggest a high-speed environment that is challenging for pedestrians to navigate safely.

hazards.name: Long crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a refuge island, increasing exposure time.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway in the foreground

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: No visible marked crosswalks at the intersection or mid-block areas, reducing driver awareness of pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb may block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a wide roadway with multiple travel lanes and no visible crossing infrastructure at the intersection. While sidewalks are present, the lack of marked crosswalks, signals, or traffic calming measures creates a high-exposure environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: The intersection lacks any painted crosswalks, providing no designated or protected space for pedestrians to cross the wide roadway.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the corner of the intersection may block the visibility between pedestrians waiting to cross and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Curb side near the corner store

hazards.name: Wide Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The width of the roadway increases the time pedestrians are exposed to moving traffic without any refuge.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the intersection to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.
